cards.reading: Reading 99: Gregory, Wrong-Way Risk
cards.statement: A cross-currency swap with a counterparty domiciled in the country whose currency one is receiving typically exhibits general wrong-way risk.
cards.explanation: A cross-currency swap with a counterparty domiciled in the country whose currency is being received is the standard example of general wrong-way risk: a devaluation increases the exposure and simultaneously impairs the local counterparty.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Discuss the impact of collateral on wrong-way risk; identify examples of wrong-way collateral
cards.reading: Reading 99: Gregory, Wrong-Way Risk
cards.statement: In modelling wrong-way risk, jump approaches reflect the limited impact of collateralisation during market jumps.
cards.explanation: Wrong-way risk often materialises as a discontinuous jump that occurs faster than a margin call can be made and settled, so jump approaches capture the limited effectiveness of collateral during stress.
cards.originalText: Prefer jump approaches, since these reflect the limited impact of collateralisation during market jumps.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Discuss the impact of collateral on wrong-way risk; identify examples of wrong-way collateral
cards.reading: Reading 99: Gregory, Wrong-Way Risk
cards.statement: Collateral provides no mitigation of wrong-way risk under any circumstances.
cards.explanation: Collateral does provide substantial mitigation of wrong-way risk; it is simply less complete than continuous models imply, because jumps can outpace the margin process.
cards.originalText: Abandon collateral modelling altogether, since collateral provides no mitigation of wrong-way risk under any circumstances.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Discuss the impact of collateral on wrong-way risk; identify examples of wrong-way collateral
cards.reading: Reading 99: Gregory, Wrong-Way Risk
cards.statement: Wrong-way risk can be fully offset by requiring the counterparty to post collateral denominated in its own home currency.
cards.explanation: Collateral denominated in the counterparty's home currency is wrong-way collateral: its value falls in the very scenario that raises the exposure. Collateral never fully offsets wrong-way risk.
cards.originalText: Accept wrong-way risk in all cases, since it can be fully offset by requiring the counterparty to post collateral denominated in its own home currency.
cards.correction: Wrong-way risk cannot be fully offset by requiring the counterparty to post collateral denominated in its own home currency.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Discuss the impact of wrong-way risk on central counterparties (CCPs)
cards.reading: Reading 99: Gregory, Wrong-Way Risk
cards.statement: A central counterparty can eliminate its own exposure to wrong-way risk entirely by transferring all wrong-way risk to clearing members through a loss allocation mechanism.
cards.explanation: Loss mutualisation reallocates losses to surviving clearing members rather than eliminating them, and can propagate stress across members. A CCP's wrong-way risk is not eliminated entirely.
cards.originalText: Transfer all wrong-way risk to clearing members through a loss allocation mechanism, since this eliminates the CCP's own exposure entirely.
cards.correction: A central counterparty cannot eliminate its own exposure to wrong-way risk entirely by transferring all wrong-way risk to clearing members through a loss allocation mechanism.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an ISDA master agreement
cards.reading: Reading 94: Gregory, ISDA Master Agreement, Netting and Close-out
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement defines the general terms between the parties with respect to matters such as netting, collateral, the definition of default, and the conditions for termination of the agreement.
cards.explanation: The ISDA Master Agreement is a single overarching contract governing all trades between two parties, setting out netting, events of default, termination and close-out mechanics; collateral terms are governed by its Credit Support Annex.
cards.originalText: It defines the general terms between the parties with respect to matters such as netting, collateral, the definition of default, and the conditions for termination of the agreement.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an ISDA master agreement
cards.reading: Reading 94: Gregory, ISDA Master Agreement, Netting and Close-out
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement defines the general terms between the parties and specifies only the conditions that may lead to termination of the contract.
cards.explanation: Termination conditions are only one element. The ISDA Master Agreement also establishes netting, its most important legal function, along with events of default and collateral arrangements.
cards.originalText: It defines the general terms between the parties and specifies only the conditions that may lead to termination of the contract.
cards.correction: The ISDA Master Agreement defines the general terms between the parties and also specifies the conditions that may lead to termination of the contract.

cards.reading: Reading 94: Gregory, ISDA Master Agreement, Netting and Close-out
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement defines the general terms between the parties and also specifies the conditions that may lead to termination of the contract.
cards.explanation: Termination conditions are only one element. The ISDA Master Agreement also establishes netting, its most important legal function, along with events of default and collateral arrangements.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an ISDA master agreement
cards.reading: Reading 94: Gregory, ISDA Master Agreement, Netting and Close-out
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement sets out the conditions under which both parties may terminate the contract with no loss or legal consequence to either side.
cards.explanation: Termination under an ISDA Master Agreement produces a close-out amount owed by one party to the other, computed at market value; it is not free of loss or legal consequence.
cards.originalText: It sets out the conditions under which both parties may terminate the contract with no loss or legal consequence to either side.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: In a credit support annex, the threshold is the level of exposure above which collateral must be posted; the minimum transfer amount is the smallest transfer that will be made, to avoid uneconomic calls; the haircut reduces the value given to posted securities; and the independent amount is posted irrespective of exposure.
cards.explanation: Each CSA parameter has a distinct role: the threshold creates uncollateralised exposure, the minimum transfer amount avoids uneconomic calls, the haircut buffers collateral price risk, and the independent amount provides overcollateralisation regardless of exposure.
cards.originalText: The threshold is the level of exposure above which collateral must be posted; the minimum transfer amount is the smallest transfer that will be made, to avoid uneconomic calls; the haircut reduces the value given to posted securities; and the independent amount is posted irrespective of exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: In a credit support annex, the threshold is the smallest transfer that will be made; the minimum transfer amount is the level of exposure above which collateral must be posted; the haircut increases the value given to posted securities; and the independent amount is posted only once exposure exceeds the threshold.
cards.explanation: The threshold is the exposure level above which collateral must be posted and the minimum transfer amount is the smallest transfer made. A haircut reduces the value given to posted securities, and the independent amount is posted irrespective of exposure.
cards.originalText: The threshold is the smallest transfer that will be made; the minimum transfer amount is the level of exposure above which collateral must be posted; the haircut increases the value given to posted securities; and the independent amount is posted only once exposure exceeds the threshold.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: In a credit support annex, the threshold is the level of exposure above which collateral must be posted; the minimum transfer amount is the smallest transfer that will be made; the haircut reduces the value given to posted securities; and the independent amount is returned as soon as exposure falls to zero.
cards.explanation: The independent amount is held throughout the life of the agreement to cover gap risk between margin calls, making it the bilateral analogue of initial margin; it is not returned when exposure falls to zero.

cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: The threshold, minimum transfer amount and haircut are all set to zero under a two-way credit support annex, since both parties post collateral symmetrically.
cards.explanation: A two-way CSA only means both parties may be required to post, depending on which way the mark-to-market runs. Thresholds, minimum transfer amounts and haircuts remain negotiable and are typically non-zero.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: A bank faces funding liquidity risk when it must post additional high-quality liquid assets as collateral during market downturns, potentially producing a liquidity shortfall.
cards.explanation: Collateralisation converts credit risk into funding liquidity risk: margin calls demand high-quality liquid assets at short notice and are largest when liquidity is scarcest.
cards.originalText: The bank faces funding liquidity risk when it must post additional high-quality liquid assets as collateral during market downturns, potentially producing a liquidity shortfall.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: A bank experiences reduced funding liquidity risk as it receives more collateral, since this increases its holdings of liquid assets.
cards.explanation: Collateral received is typically segregated or subject to rehypothecation limits, so it is not freely available for funding, and it must be returned when the mark-to-market reverses. Treating it as own liquidity is a serious error.
cards.originalText: The bank experiences reduced funding liquidity risk as it receives more collateral, since this increases its holdings of liquid assets.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: Using long-term illiquid assets as collateral minimises funding liquidity risk, since such assets are not needed for day-to-day operations.
cards.explanation: Illiquid assets are generally not eligible as collateral, and where accepted carry large haircuts. Funding liquidity risk concerns the ability to deliver liquid assets on demand, which illiquid holdings do not help.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: Funding liquidity risk is eliminated by collateralisation, because posting collateral converts credit exposure into a fully secured position.
cards.explanation: Collateralisation reduces credit exposure but creates funding liquidity risk in doing so; it transforms the risk rather than eliminating it.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: In the context of collateralisation, operational risk emerges from inaccurate valuation of collateral, leading to inadequate collateral postings and disputes with counterparties.
cards.explanation: Collateral management is a high-volume, time-critical process; valuation errors, failed settlements and missed calls create operational losses that would not exist in an uncollateralised relationship.
cards.originalText: Operational risk emerges from inaccurate valuation of collateral, leading to inadequate collateral postings and disputes with counterparties.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: In collateral management, operational risk is mitigated by using diversified collateral, which reduces exposure to any single asset's volatility.
cards.explanation: Diversifying collateral addresses market risk on the collateral pool, not operational risk; holding more asset types actually increases operational complexity, since each needs its own valuation, haircut and settlement process.
cards.originalText: Operational risk is mitigated by using diversified collateral, which reduces exposure to any single asset's volatility.
cards.correction: In collateral management, market risk is mitigated by using diversified collateral, which reduces exposure to any single asset's volatility.

cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin

cards.explanation: Diversifying collateral addresses market risk on the collateral pool, not operational risk; holding more asset types actually increases operational complexity, since each needs its own valuation, haircut and settlement process.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: Operational risk is unaffected by collateralisation practices, since it is primarily concerned with market movements.
cards.explanation: Operational risk concerns failures of people, processes and systems, not market movements. Collateralisation creates operational risk through daily valuation, calls, settlement and dispute handling.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization
cards.reading: Reading 95: Gregory, Collateral and Margin
cards.statement: In collateral management, operational risk arises only when collateral is held with a third-party custodian rather than directly by the receiving party.
cards.explanation: Operational risk in collateral management arises across valuation, calls, settlement and dispute handling regardless of where the assets are held; third-party custody is not its sole source.
cards.originalText: Operational risk arises only when collateral is held with a third-party custodian rather than directly by the receiving party.
cards.correction: In collateral management, operational risk arises whether collateral is held with a third-party custodian or directly by the receiving party.

cards.explanation: Operational risk in collateral management arises across valuation, calls, settlement and dispute handling regardless of where the assets are held; third-party custody is not its sole source.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify factors that affect the calculation of the credit exposure profile and summarize the impact of collateral on exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The exposure profile of an interest rate swap reflects a diffusion effect that increases uncertainty about future value as the horizon lengthens, offset by an amortisation effect that reduces the remaining cash flows at risk as the swap approaches maturity; collateral truncates the profile at the threshold plus the exposure accruing over the margin period of risk.
cards.explanation: Diffusion (growing uncertainty) dominates early and amortisation (fewer remaining cash flows) dominates late, producing a hump-shaped swap exposure profile. Collateral caps exposure at a residual level of the threshold, minimum transfer amount and exposure accruing over the margin period of risk.
cards.originalText: A diffusion effect that increases uncertainty about future value as the horizon lengthens, offset by an amortisation effect that reduces the remaining cash flows at risk as the swap approaches maturity; collateral truncates the profile at the threshold plus the exposure accruing over the margin period of risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify factors that affect the calculation of the credit exposure profile and summarize the impact of collateral on exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The exposure profile of an interest rate swap reflects a diffusion effect that reduces uncertainty as the horizon lengthens, offset by an amortisation effect that increases the remaining cash flows at risk; collateral removes the profile entirely once a credit support annex is in place.
cards.explanation: Both effects are reversed: uncertainty grows with the horizon (diffusion), while remaining cash flows shrink toward maturity (amortisation). Collateral does not remove exposure entirely; residual exposure remains from the threshold, minimum transfer amount and margin period of risk.
cards.originalText: A diffusion effect that reduces uncertainty as the horizon lengthens, offset by an amortisation effect that increases the remaining cash flows at risk; collateral removes the profile entirely once a credit support annex is in place.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify factors that affect the calculation of the credit exposure profile and summarize the impact of collateral on exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The exposure profile of an interest rate swap reflects a diffusion effect and an amortisation effect that both increase exposure over time, producing a monotonically rising profile; collateral shifts the entire profile downward by the amount of collateral held.
cards.explanation: Diffusion increases exposure while amortisation decreases it, so a swap's exposure profile rises and then falls rather than peaking at maturity. Collateral truncates the profile at a residual level rather than shifting it down by a fixed amount.
cards.originalText: A diffusion effect and an amortisation effect that both increase exposure over time, producing a monotonically rising profile; collateral shifts the entire profile downward by the amount of collateral held.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify factors that affect the calculation of the credit exposure profile and summarize the impact of collateral on exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Under a single netting agreement, the netting advantage between two derivative positions is greatest when they have a strong positive correlation.
cards.explanation: Strongly positively correlated trades tend to be in the money together, leaving little to offset, so the netting benefit is smallest. The benefit is greatest when trades are strongly negatively correlated.
cards.originalText: The currency swap and the interest rate swap have a strong positive correlation.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify factors that affect the calculation of the credit exposure profile and summarize the impact of collateral on exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Under a single netting agreement, the netting advantage between two derivative positions is greatest when they have a strong negative correlation.
cards.explanation: Netting only helps when trades take opposite signs. Strongly negatively correlated trades are in opposite states most of the time, so the offset is frequent and large.
cards.originalText: The currency swap and the interest rate swap have a strong negative correlation.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify typical credit exposure profiles for various derivative contracts and combination profiles
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: A plain vanilla interest rate swap is the instrument most likely to exhibit a bell-shaped or humped potential future exposure profile over time.
cards.explanation: Early in a swap's life diffusion dominates as rate uncertainty builds, and later amortisation dominates as few cash flows remain, so the profile peaks roughly one third of the way through and falls to zero at maturity.
cards.originalText: A plain vanilla interest rate swap

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Shortening the remargining period will decrease operational costs by reducing the frequency of collateral adjustments.
cards.explanation: Shortening the remargining period increases the frequency of collateral adjustments and therefore raises operational cost, while reducing exposure.
cards.correction: Shortening the remargining period will increase operational costs by increasing the frequency of collateral adjustments.

cards.statement: Shortening the remargining period will increase operational costs by increasing the frequency of collateral adjustments.
cards.explanation: Shortening the remargining period increases the frequency of collateral adjustments and therefore raises operational cost, while reducing exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: A shorter remargining period will increase exposure to market volatility and counterparty risk.
cards.explanation: A shorter remargining period means less time for a position to move uncollateralised, so counterparty exposure falls rather than rises.
cards.correction: A shorter remargining period will decrease exposure to market volatility and counterparty risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: A shorter remargining period will decrease exposure to market volatility and counterparty risk.
cards.explanation: A shorter remargining period means less time for a position to move uncollateralised, so counterparty exposure falls rather than rises.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Reducing the remargining period will decrease exposure, because less time elapses during which the position can move against the firm before collateral is called and received.
cards.explanation: Exposure accruing over the margin period of risk grows roughly with the square root of its length, so shortening the remargining period reduces the residual uncollateralised exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The remargining period has no effect on exposure, since the threshold and minimum transfer amount determine the residual entirely.
cards.explanation: Residual exposure has three components: the threshold, the minimum transfer amount, and exposure accruing over the margin period of risk. The remargining period directly governs the third.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Increasing the collateral threshold will reduce credit risk, by requiring more collateral to be posted and thus providing greater protection.
cards.explanation: The threshold is subtracted in the credit support amount calculation, so increasing it requires less collateral, not more, and raises uncollateralised exposure and credit risk.
cards.originalText: Increasing the threshold will reduce credit risk, by requiring more collateral to be posted and thus providing greater protection.
cards.correction: Lowering the collateral threshold will reduce credit risk, by requiring more collateral to be posted and thus providing greater protection.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Lowering the collateral threshold will reduce credit risk, by requiring more collateral to be posted and thus providing greater protection.
cards.explanation: The threshold is subtracted in the credit support amount calculation, so increasing it requires less collateral, not more, and raises uncollateralised exposure and credit risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Lowering the collateral threshold will reduce credit risk, by requiring collateral to be posted for smaller changes in exposure.
cards.explanation: The threshold acts as an unsecured credit line; lowering it means collateral is called for smaller exposures, reducing uncollateralised exposure at the cost of higher operational burden.
cards.originalText: Lowering the threshold will reduce credit risk, by requiring collateral to be posted for smaller changes in exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Changing the collateral threshold has no significant impact on credit risk but affects the operational efficiency of managing collateral.
cards.explanation: The threshold is the largest contractual determinant of residual uncollateralised exposure; raising it increases credit risk one for one, so its credit impact is significant, not only operational.
cards.originalText: Changing the threshold has no significant impact on credit risk but affects the operational efficiency of managing collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: A higher collateral threshold decreases the frequency of collateral calls, thereby decreasing credit risk while reducing administrative costs.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold does reduce the frequency of collateral calls and administrative costs, but it leaves more exposure uncollateralised and therefore increases credit risk.
cards.originalText: A higher threshold decreases the frequency of collateral calls, thereby decreasing credit risk while reducing administrative costs.
cards.correction: A higher collateral threshold decreases the frequency of collateral calls, thereby increasing credit risk while reducing administrative costs.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: A higher collateral threshold decreases the frequency of collateral calls, thereby increasing credit risk while reducing administrative costs.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold does reduce the frequency of collateral calls and administrative costs, but it leaves more exposure uncollateralised and therefore increases credit risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The minimum transfer amount prevents uneconomic transfers of trivial sums, and it adds directly to the uncollateralised exposure, since exposure can move by up to that amount without triggering a call.
cards.explanation: The minimum transfer amount suppresses calls below an agreed size to avoid uneconomic transfers, and the suppressed amount is uncollateralised, adding to the threshold in its effect on residual exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The minimum transfer amount is the smallest exposure at which collateral becomes payable, so it performs the same function as the threshold and the two should be set equal.
cards.explanation: The threshold suppresses collateralisation below a level of exposure; the minimum transfer amount suppresses transfers below a certain size at all exposure levels. They perform different functions and need not be equal.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The minimum transfer amount reduces uncollateralised exposure, because it guarantees that any transfer made is at least that size.
cards.explanation: Requiring transfers to be at least a certain size means small exposure movements are not collateralised at all, which increases rather than reduces uncollateralised exposure.
cards.correction: The minimum transfer amount increases uncollateralised exposure, because it guarantees that any transfer made is at least that size.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The minimum transfer amount increases uncollateralised exposure, because it guarantees that any transfer made is at least that size.
cards.explanation: Requiring transfers to be at least a certain size means small exposure movements are not collateralised at all, which increases rather than reduces uncollateralised exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: The minimum transfer amount affects only the rounding of collateral transfers and has no bearing on residual exposure.
cards.explanation: Rounding is a separate, much smaller convention applied to the size of a transfer once triggered. The minimum transfer amount determines whether a transfer happens at all and adds directly to residual exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Both current and future counterparty exposure of a derivative position are not known with certainty.
cards.explanation: Current exposure is known with certainty because it is computed from observable market prices today. Only future exposure is uncertain.
cards.originalText: Both current and future exposure are not known with certainty.
cards.correction: Only future counterparty exposure of a derivative position is not known with certainty.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Only future counterparty exposure of a derivative position is not known with certainty.
cards.explanation: Current exposure is known with certainty because it is computed from observable market prices today. Only future exposure is uncertain.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Future counterparty exposure of a derivative position can be predicted from past and present exposure.
cards.explanation: Future exposure depends on market movements that have not yet occurred, so it cannot be extrapolated from the realised path; it is simulated and described probabilistically.
cards.originalText: Future exposure can be predicted from past and present exposure.
cards.correction: Future counterparty exposure of a derivative position cannot be predicted from past and present exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Future counterparty exposure of a derivative position cannot be predicted from past and present exposure.
cards.explanation: Future exposure depends on market movements that have not yet occurred, so it cannot be extrapolated from the realised path; it is simulated and described probabilistically.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: While current and past counterparty exposure are known with certainty, future exposure is largely uncertain and can only be characterised by probabilistic estimates of future market movements.
cards.explanation: Past and current exposure are computed from observed market data, whereas future exposure depends on unrealised market movements and can only be described as a distribution.
cards.originalText: While current and past exposure are known with certainty, future exposure is largely uncertain and can only be characterised by probabilistic estimates of future market movements.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: While past counterparty exposure is known with certainty, current and future exposure are uncertain and subject to probabilistic estimates.
cards.explanation: Today's mark-to-market is observable, so current exposure is known with certainty. Only future exposure is uncertain and described probabilistically.
cards.originalText: While past exposure is known with certainty, current and future exposure are uncertain and subject to probabilistic estimates.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Current exposure is today's positive mark-to-market; peak exposure is a high quantile of exposure at a future date; expected exposure is the mean of exposure at a future date; and expected positive exposure is the time average of expected exposure over a horizon.
cards.explanation: Current exposure is an observed value today; peak exposure is a high quantile at a single future date; expected exposure is the mean at a single future date; expected positive exposure averages expected exposure across the horizon.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Current exposure is today's positive mark-to-market; peak exposure is the mean of exposure at a future date; expected exposure is a high quantile at a future date; and expected positive exposure is the maximum of expected exposure over a horizon.
cards.explanation: Peak exposure is a high quantile and expected exposure is a mean at a future date, not the reverse. Expected positive exposure is the time average of expected exposure, not its maximum.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate among current exposure, peak exposure, expected exposure, and expected positive exposure
cards.reading: Reading 97: Gregory, Credit Exposure and Funding
cards.statement: Expected exposure and expected positive exposure are identical, since exposure is floored at zero and therefore always positive; the two terms are used interchangeably in practice.
cards.explanation: Expected exposure is a profile through time and expected positive exposure is its time average over a horizon, so the two differ whenever the profile is not flat.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the treatment of counterparty credit risk both as a credit risk and as a market risk and describe its implications for trading activities and risk management
cards.reading: Reading 93: Counterparty Credit Risk
cards.statement: Counterparty credit risk is a credit risk because the loss is triggered by counterparty default, and a market risk because the size of that loss depends on market-driven exposure; the practical implication is that CVA must be priced into trades and hedged with market instruments, so a dedicated CVA desk sits between the trading desks and the counterparty.
cards.explanation: Default supplies the trigger for a loss and market movements supply its magnitude through exposure at default. So CVA must be priced into trades and hedged with market instruments, typically by a dedicated CVA desk.
cards.originalText: It is a credit risk because the loss is triggered by counterparty default, and a market risk because the size of that loss depends on market-driven exposure; the practical implication is that CVA must be priced into trades and hedged with market instruments, so a dedicated CVA desk sits between the trading desks and the counterparty.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the treatment of counterparty credit risk both as a credit risk and as a market risk and describe its implications for trading activities and risk management
cards.reading: Reading 93: Counterparty Credit Risk
cards.statement: Counterparty credit risk is a credit risk only, since the loss requires a default event; market factors affect the timing of default but not the size of the loss, so the credit function should own it exclusively.
cards.explanation: Market factors determine the size of the exposure at default, not merely the timing of default. That is what distinguishes a derivative exposure from a loan and why exposure must be simulated.
cards.originalText: It is a credit risk only, since the loss requires a default event; market factors affect the timing of default but not the size of the loss, so the credit function should own it exclusively.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the treatment of counterparty credit risk both as a credit risk and as a market risk and describe its implications for trading activities and risk management
cards.reading: Reading 93: Counterparty Credit Risk
cards.statement: Counterparty credit risk is a market risk only, since exposure is marked to market daily; default is already captured in the credit spread used to discount the position, so no separate credit treatment is required.
cards.explanation: Marking to market measures current value, not the loss on default. The loss requires a default event, and its size depends on exposure at the future moment of default, so counterparty risk has a credit dimension as well as a market one.
cards.originalText: It is a market risk only, since exposure is marked to market daily; default is already captured in the credit spread used to discount the position, so no separate credit treatment is required.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the treatment of counterparty credit risk both as a credit risk and as a market risk and describe its implications for trading activities and risk management
cards.reading: Reading 93: Counterparty Credit Risk
cards.statement: Counterparty credit risk is treated as both a credit and a market risk, but the two treatments are alternatives rather than complements: an institution using CVA for pricing should not also hold regulatory capital against counterparty exposure, since this double counts the same risk.
cards.explanation: CVA pricing and regulatory capital are complements, not alternatives. Basel III requires capital for counterparty default risk and a separate CVA capital charge, because CVA itself is volatile.
cards.originalText: It is treated as both, but the two treatments are alternatives rather than complements: an institution using CVA for pricing should not also hold regulatory capital against counterparty exposure, since this double counts the same risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the treatment of counterparty credit risk both as a credit risk and as a market risk and describe its implications for trading activities and risk management
cards.reading: Reading 93: Counterparty Credit Risk
cards.statement: Settlement risk is significantly more likely to occur than pre-settlement risk.
cards.explanation: Settlement risk exists only during a short settlement window of hours or days, whereas pre-settlement risk is present over the entire life of the contract, so settlement risk is materially less likely to occur.
cards.correction: Settlement risk is significantly less likely to occur than pre-settlement risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the treatment of counterparty credit risk both as a credit risk and as a market risk and describe its implications for trading activities and risk management
cards.reading: Reading 93: Counterparty Credit Risk
cards.statement: Settlement risk is significantly less likely to occur than pre-settlement risk.
cards.explanation: Settlement risk exists only during a short settlement window of hours or days, whereas pre-settlement risk is present over the entire life of the contract, so settlement risk is materially less likely to occur.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the treatment of counterparty credit risk both as a credit risk and as a market risk and describe its implications for trading activities and risk management
cards.reading: Reading 93: Counterparty Credit Risk
cards.statement: Settlement risk and pre-settlement risk have broadly equal probabilities of occurrence.
cards.explanation: Pre-settlement risk runs for the whole life of the contract, potentially years, while settlement risk lasts only hours or days, so pre-settlement risk is substantially more likely to occur.
cards.originalText: Both types of risk have broadly equal probabilities of occurrence.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the treatment of counterparty credit risk both as a credit risk and as a market risk and describe its implications for trading activities and risk management
cards.reading: Reading 93: Counterparty Credit Risk
cards.statement: Pre-settlement risk is significantly more likely to occur than default at the settlement date.
cards.explanation: Pre-settlement risk is present from trade date to maturity, while settlement risk is confined to the short settlement window. Settlement risk can, however, involve the full principal of the delivered leg.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Estimate risk-weighted assets and capital adequacy ratio of a financial institution
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: Under the Basel standardised approach for credit risk, a bank must obtain regulatory approval for its internal risk models.
cards.explanation: Supervisory approval of internal models is a requirement of the internal ratings-based approaches. Under the standardised approach there are no internal models to approve.
cards.originalText: Obtain regulatory approval for its internal risk models.
cards.correction: Under the Basel internal ratings-based approach for credit risk, a bank must obtain regulatory approval for its internal risk models.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Estimate risk-weighted assets and capital adequacy ratio of a financial institution
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: Under the Basel internal ratings-based approach for credit risk, a bank must obtain regulatory approval for its internal risk models.
cards.explanation: Supervisory approval of internal models is a requirement of the internal ratings-based approaches. Under the standardised approach there are no internal models to approve.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Estimate risk-weighted assets and capital adequacy ratio of a financial institution
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: Under the Basel standardised approach for credit risk, a bank assigns predefined risk weights to its assets as set by regulatory authorities.
cards.explanation: Under the standardised approach the regulator prescribes risk weights directly, so the bank applies them to its asset classes rather than estimating its own risk parameters.
cards.originalText: Assign predefined risk weights to its assets as set by regulatory authorities.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Estimate risk-weighted assets and capital adequacy ratio of a financial institution
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: Under the Basel standardised approach for credit risk, a bank calculates the probability of default for each type of asset.
cards.explanation: Estimating probability of default for each exposure is a defining feature of the internal ratings-based approaches. The standardised approach uses regulator-prescribed risk weights instead.
cards.originalText: Calculate the probability of default for each type of asset.
cards.correction: Under the Basel internal ratings-based approach for credit risk, a bank calculates the probability of default for each type of asset.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Estimate risk-weighted assets and capital adequacy ratio of a financial institution
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: Under the Basel internal ratings-based approach for credit risk, a bank calculates the probability of default for each type of asset.
cards.explanation: Estimating probability of default for each exposure is a defining feature of the internal ratings-based approaches. The standardised approach uses regulator-prescribed risk weights instead.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how the credit loss distribution is modeled
cards.reading: Reading 82: Schroeck, Capital Structure in Banks
cards.statement: The beta distribution is symmetric for all values of alpha and beta, and can only be made skewed by adding a third parameter.
cards.explanation: The beta distribution is symmetric only when alpha equals beta, and it produces skew with its existing two parameters; no third parameter is required.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how the credit loss distribution is modeled
cards.reading: Reading 82: Schroeck, Capital Structure in Banks
cards.statement: The beta distribution is a continuous approximation of a binomial distribution, that is, of the sum of independent two point distributions.
cards.explanation: The beta distribution is the continuous analogue of a binomial, which suits credit portfolios because they are sums of two-point outcomes (default or no default).

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how the credit loss distribution is modeled
cards.reading: Reading 82: Schroeck, Capital Structure in Banks
cards.statement: When modelling extreme credit losses using the beta distribution, Monte Carlo simulation is typically employed to complement it, so as to account for a wider range of potential outcomes in the tail.
cards.explanation: The beta is fitted from two moments, which calibrates the body of the loss distribution; Monte Carlo simulation populates the extreme tail, where economic capital is read, by generating many joint default scenarios.
cards.originalText: Monte Carlo simulation, to account for a wider range of potential outcomes.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe challenges to quantifying credit risk
cards.reading: Reading 82: Schroeck, Capital Structure in Banks
cards.statement: The bottom-up approach to quantifying economic capital for credit risk assumes that credits are illiquid assets.
cards.explanation: The illiquidity assumption is a stated caveat of the bottom-up approach: the model captures only internal risk contributions to the existing credit portfolio, not correlations as priced in liquid markets.
cards.originalText: The approach assumes that credits are illiquid assets.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe challenges to quantifying credit risk
cards.reading: Reading 82: Schroeck, Capital Structure in Banks
cards.statement: In practice, to avoid undue complexity, internal credit risk models tend to use only a one year estimation horizon rather than a multi period horizon.
cards.explanation: Almost all internal credit risk models use a one-year horizon, which ignores the multi-period nature of credit and the correlated migration of credit quality over time.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe challenges to quantifying credit risk
cards.reading: Reading 82: Schroeck, Capital Structure in Banks
cards.statement: While the bottom-up approach to quantifying economic capital for credit risk considers default correlation within the same risk type, it assumes that market and operational risk components are separated and are measured and managed in different departments within the bank.
cards.explanation: The bottom-up approach considers correlations only within the credit risk type and assumes market and operational risk are measured and managed separately elsewhere in the bank.
cards.originalText: While the approach considers default correlation within the same risk type, it assumes that market and operational risk components are separated and are measured and managed in different departments within the bank.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the judgmental approaches, empirical models, and financial models to predict default
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: Linear discriminant analysis produces a non-linear scoring function.
cards.explanation: Linear discriminant analysis produces a linear scoring function, a weighted sum of explanatory variables. Non-linear alternatives such as logistic regression or quadratic discriminant analysis are different techniques.
cards.originalText: The analysis produces a non-linear scoring function.
cards.correction: Linear discriminant analysis produces a linear scoring function.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the judgmental approaches, empirical models, and financial models to predict default
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: Linear discriminant analysis produces a linear scoring function.
cards.explanation: Linear discriminant analysis produces a linear scoring function, a weighted sum of explanatory variables. Non-linear alternatives such as logistic regression or quadratic discriminant analysis are different techniques.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the judgmental approaches, empirical models, and financial models to predict default
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: In linear discriminant analysis, variables are selected from a large set of accounting ratios, qualitative features and judgments, with little regard to their statistical significance.
cards.explanation: Variable selection in linear discriminant analysis is driven by statistical discriminating power. Choosing variables with little regard to statistical significance describes a judgmental approach.
cards.originalText: Variables are selected from a large set of accounting ratios, qualitative features and judgments, with little regard to their statistical significance.
cards.correction: In linear discriminant analysis, variables are selected from a large set of accounting ratios, qualitative features and judgments, based on their statistical significance.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the judgmental approaches, empirical models, and financial models to predict default
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: In linear discriminant analysis, variables are selected from a large set of accounting ratios, qualitative features and judgments, based on their statistical significance.
cards.explanation: Variable selection in linear discriminant analysis is driven by statistical discriminating power. Choosing variables with little regard to statistical significance describes a judgmental approach.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the judgmental approaches, empirical models, and financial models to predict default
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: In linear discriminant analysis, the score produced by the function must lie between 0 and 1.
cards.explanation: A discriminant score such as Altman's Z-score is unbounded and unitless, not a probability. Output constrained between 0 and 1 is a feature of logistic regression.
cards.originalText: The score produced by the function must lie between 0 and 1.
cards.correction: In linear discriminant analysis, the score produced by the function need not lie between 0 and 1.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the judgmental approaches, empirical models, and financial models to predict default
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: In linear discriminant analysis, the score produced by the function need not lie between 0 and 1.
cards.explanation: A discriminant score such as Altman's Z-score is unbounded and unitless, not a probability. Output constrained between 0 and 1 is a feature of logistic regression.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the judgmental approaches, empirical models, and financial models to predict default
cards.reading: Reading 83: Doumpos, Fundamentals of Credit Risk
cards.statement: In linear discriminant analysis, when a good discriminant function has been estimated using historical data on performing and defaulted borrowers, any new borrower can be assigned to a predefined group based on the score the function produces.
cards.explanation: Linear discriminant analysis estimates weights that best separate known groups in a historical sample; a new borrower's score is then compared with a cut-off to assign group membership.
cards.originalText: When a good discriminant function has been estimated using historical data on performing and defaulted borrowers, any new borrower can be assigned to a predefined group based on the score the function produces.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Compare agencies' ratings to internal credit rating systems
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Internal ratings can provide a more detailed evaluation of a company's ability to service its debt through specific financial metrics and cash flow analysis.
cards.explanation: Internal rating systems can use full borrower relationship data, cash flow and facility detail, giving a depth of analysis that a standardised agency methodology based on public disclosure does not reach.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Compare agencies' ratings to internal credit rating systems
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Agency ratings offer more consistent results because they are applied uniformly across industries and geographic regions.
cards.explanation: Uniform application across industries and regions gives agency ratings high comparability; this is an advantage of agency ratings over institution-specific internal ratings.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Compare agencies' ratings to internal credit rating systems
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Internal ratings are generally more accessible to the public and provide a broader understanding of a company's financial health.
cards.explanation: Internal ratings are proprietary and not public; agency ratings are the ones that are published.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the relationship between borrower rating and probability of default
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Default probability rises non-linearly across the rating scale, so that each step down represents a progressively larger absolute increase in PD; a rating is therefore an ordinal ranking that must be calibrated to a PD before it can be used in pricing or capital.
cards.explanation: One-year default rates rise geometrically across rating grades, so each notch down multiplies rather than adds to PD. Ratings are ordinal and must be calibrated to a PD before quantitative use.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the relationship between borrower rating and probability of default
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Default probability rises linearly across the rating scale, so that the PD difference between AAA and AA equals the difference between B and CCC, which is what makes rating grades comparable.
cards.explanation: Default probabilities rise geometrically, not linearly, across the rating scale; the step from B to CCC adds far more PD than the step from AAA to AA.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the relationship between borrower rating and probability of default
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: A rating grade is itself a probability of default expressed on a letter scale, so no separate calibration is required before it can be used in a capital calculation.
cards.explanation: A rating is an ordinal grade, not a probability. It must be calibrated to a numeric PD before it can be used in pricing or a capital formula.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the relationship between borrower rating and probability of default
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Default probability is unrelated to the rating grade over short horizons, because ratings are assigned through the cycle and therefore describe long-run average behaviour only.
cards.explanation: Through-the-cycle ratings map to cycle-average default probabilities that remain informative every year; realised default rates vary around that mapping rather than being unrelated to the grade.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify drawbacks in using the correlation-based credit portfolio framework
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: In a correlation-based credit portfolio framework, default correlations are very difficult to estimate because joint defaults are rare and credits are illiquid; the Gaussian copula understates tail dependence, so simultaneous extreme defaults are less likely under the model than in reality; and results are highly sensitive to a parameter that cannot be observed.
cards.explanation: The correlation parameter that drives the tail is unobservable and sparsely estimated, the Gaussian copula assigns near independence to extreme joint outcomes, and small changes in correlation move credit VaR materially.
cards.originalText: Default correlations are very difficult to estimate because joint defaults are rare and credits are illiquid; the Gaussian copula understates tail dependence, so simultaneous extreme defaults are less likely under the model than in reality; and results are highly sensitive to a parameter that cannot be observed.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify drawbacks in using the correlation-based credit portfolio framework
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: In a correlation-based credit portfolio framework, default correlations are readily observable from equity markets, so the framework's weakness is computational cost rather than parameter uncertainty; the Gaussian copula overstates tail dependence and therefore produces conservative capital numbers.
cards.explanation: Default correlations are not readily observable, so parameter uncertainty is a core weakness. The Gaussian copula understates tail dependence, making the framework optimistic rather than conservative in the tail.
cards.originalText: Default correlations are readily observable from equity markets, so the framework's weakness is computational cost rather than parameter uncertainty; the Gaussian copula overstates tail dependence and therefore produces conservative capital numbers.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify drawbacks in using the correlation-based credit portfolio framework
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: The principal drawback of a correlation-based credit portfolio framework is that it cannot accommodate portfolios with more than a few hundred exposures, since the correlation matrix grows factorially with the number of names.
cards.explanation: The number of correlation pairs grows quadratically, not factorially, and factor models reduce the parameters to one loading per name. Portfolio size is an inconvenience; the principal weaknesses are parameter uncertainty and understated tail dependence.
cards.originalText: The framework's principal drawback is that it cannot accommodate portfolios with more than a few hundred exposures, since the correlation matrix grows factorially with the number of names.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify drawbacks in using the correlation-based credit portfolio framework
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: A correlation-based credit portfolio framework has no material drawbacks for portfolios of investment-grade credits, since default correlations for high-quality names are close to zero and the resulting loss distribution is approximately normal.
cards.explanation: Investment-grade default correlations are low but not zero, credit loss distributions are skewed rather than approximately normal, and senior high-quality exposures are the most sensitive to the correlation assumption.
cards.originalText: The framework has no material drawbacks for portfolios of investment-grade credits, since default correlations for high-quality names are close to zero and the resulting loss distribution is approximately normal.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe how Credit VaR can be calculated using a simulation of joint defaults; describe the use of a single factor model to measure portfolio credit risk
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Portfolio credit VaR can be obtained by computing each name's standalone credit VaR analytically and summing them, since credit VaR is additive across exposures within a portfolio.
cards.explanation: Credit VaR is sub-additive for a diversified portfolio, so summing standalone figures overstates portfolio risk and eliminates the diversification benefit.
cards.originalText: Compute each name's standalone credit VaR analytically and sum them, since credit VaR is additive across exposures within a portfolio.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe recovery rates and their dependencies on default rates
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Recovery rates increase as default rates increase, because more defaults provide more data for improving recovery strategies.
cards.explanation: Recovery rates fall as default rates rise. More default observations may improve future modelling, but they cannot raise contemporaneous recovery prices.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe recovery rates and their dependencies on default rates
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Recovery rates decrease as default rates increase, due to market saturation with defaulted securities and reduced asset valuations.
cards.explanation: Recovery and default rates are negatively correlated: a downturn floods the market with distressed assets facing limited buyers, and the same conditions depress collateral and asset values.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe recovery rates and their dependencies on default rates
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Recovery rates are independent of default rates, being determined solely by the original credit rating of the bond issue.
cards.explanation: Empirical evidence shows recovery rates are negatively correlated with default rates. Assuming independence understates downturn losses; the original rating does not insulate realised recovery from the cycle.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe recovery rates and their dependencies on default rates
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: Recovery rates and default rates are inversely proportional, due to the high liquidity of defaulting securities in economic downturns.
cards.explanation: The relationship is a negative empirical correlation, not a fixed inverse proportionality, and defaulted securities are illiquid rather than highly liquid in downturns; illiquidity is part of why recovery prices fall.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the default probabilities used to value a CDS; describe the valuation of a synthetic CDO
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: In valuing a synthetic CDO tranche, the spread payments approach equates the present value of the premium leg received by the protection seller with the present value of the expected protection payments on the tranche, and the Gaussian copula is used to generate correlated default times across the reference portfolio so that the tranche loss distribution can be simulated.
cards.explanation: A synthetic CDO tranche is priced by setting the spread that equates the premium and protection legs, and the protection leg needs a tranche loss distribution generated by simulating correlated default times through a Gaussian copula.
cards.originalText: The spread payments approach equates the present value of the premium leg received by the protection seller with the present value of the expected protection payments on the tranche, and the Gaussian copula is used to generate correlated default times across the reference portfolio so that the tranche loss distribution can be simulated.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the default probabilities used to value a CDS; describe the valuation of a synthetic CDO
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: In valuing a synthetic CDO tranche, the spread payments approach discounts the tranche's coupon at the risk-free rate and ignores default, while the Gaussian copula is used to calibrate the recovery rate assumption for each reference name.
cards.explanation: Ignoring default would value the tranche as a risk-free bond. The Gaussian copula generates correlated default times across the reference portfolio; it is not a recovery calibration device.
cards.originalText: The spread payments approach discounts the tranche's coupon at the risk-free rate and ignores default, while the Gaussian copula is used to calibrate the recovery rate assumption for each reference name.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the default probabilities used to value a CDS; describe the valuation of a synthetic CDO
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: In valuing a synthetic CDO tranche, the spread payments approach and the Gaussian copula are alternatives that produce identical values by construction, since the copula is simply a numerical implementation of the spread payments identity.
cards.explanation: The spread payments approach is the valuation identity, and the Gaussian copula is the method that populates the loss distribution the identity requires. One is the equation, the other supplies its input.
cards.originalText: The two approaches are alternatives that produce identical values by construction, since the copula is simply a numerical implementation of the spread payments identity.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the default probabilities used to value a CDS; describe the valuation of a synthetic CDO
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: In valuing a synthetic CDO tranche, the Gaussian copula generates independent default times for each reference name, and the spread payments approach then aggregates them, so that tranche value depends on the individual default probabilities but not on any correlation assumption.
cards.explanation: The copula's purpose is to introduce dependence between default times. Tranche values, especially senior and equity tranches, are highly sensitive to the correlation assumption.
cards.originalText: The Gaussian copula generates independent default times for each reference name, and the spread payments approach then aggregates them, so that tranche value depends on the individual default probabilities but not on any correlation assumption.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Assess the credit risks of derivatives
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: When valuing a credit default swap on which protection has been bought, the risk-free value of the swap is reduced by a CVA term reflecting the joint event that the protection seller defaults while the swap has positive value to the buyer, and the adjustment is larger the higher the correlation between the seller and the reference entity.
cards.explanation: A purchased CDS is most valuable when credit conditions have deteriorated, which is when a correlated protection seller is least able to pay. This wrong-way risk raises the CVA as seller-reference correlation rises.
cards.originalText: The risk-free value of the swap is reduced by a CVA term reflecting the joint event that the protection seller defaults while the swap has positive value to the buyer, and the adjustment is larger the higher the correlation between the seller and the reference entity.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Assess the credit risks of derivatives
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: When valuing a credit default swap on which protection has been bought, the risk-free value is reduced by a CVA term computed from the seller's default probability alone, since the correlation between the seller and the reference entity affects the timing of the loss but not its size.
cards.explanation: Correlation between the protection seller and the reference entity affects the size of the expected loss, because the relevant quantity is exposure conditional on seller default. This is the wrong-way risk the adjustment must capture.
cards.originalText: The risk-free value is reduced by a CVA term computed from the seller's default probability alone, since the correlation between the seller and the reference entity affects the timing of the loss but not its size.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Assess the credit risks of derivatives
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: No adjustment for the protection seller's credit risk is required when valuing a purchased credit default swap, because a credit default swap is collateralised by definition and the protection buyer's exposure is therefore always zero.
cards.explanation: Credit default swaps are not collateralised by definition, and even fully collateralised positions retain residual exposure through the threshold, minimum transfer amount and margin period of risk.
cards.originalText: No adjustment is required, because a credit default swap is collateralised by definition and the protection buyer's exposure is therefore always zero.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Assess the credit risks of derivatives
cards.reading: Reading 88: Hull, Estimating Default Probabilities
cards.statement: When valuing a credit default swap on which protection has been bought, the risk-free value is increased by a DVA term reflecting the buyer's own default probability, and no adjustment is made for the seller, since the buyer bears no exposure to the seller once the premium has been paid.
cards.explanation: The protection buyer is exposed to the seller for the life of the contract, since premiums are paid periodically and the contingent payout lies in the future. DVA reflects the buyer's own default and does not remove the need for CVA.
cards.originalText: The risk-free value is increased by a DVA term reflecting the buyer's own default probability, and no adjustment is made for the seller, since the buyer bears no exposure to the seller once the premium has been paid.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement
cards.reading: Reading 94: Gregory, ISDA Master Agreement, Netting and Close-out
cards.statement: Payment netting reduces settlement risk by combining same-day, same-currency cash flows, while close-out netting reduces credit exposure on default by collapsing all transactions in the netting set to a single net amount; close-out netting depends on enforceability in the counterparty's jurisdiction, and multilateral netting across three or more parties generally requires a central counterparty.
cards.explanation: Payment netting addresses settlement risk and close-out netting addresses default exposure. Legal enforceability in the relevant jurisdiction is the binding constraint, and genuine multilateral netting requires all participants to face a common counterparty such as a CCP.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement
cards.reading: Reading 94: Gregory, ISDA Master Agreement, Netting and Close-out
cards.statement: Payment netting reduces credit exposure on default while close-out netting reduces settlement risk on a daily basis; both are automatically enforceable in every jurisdiction because they are contained in a standard-form agreement.
cards.explanation: The functions are transposed: payment netting addresses settlement risk and close-out netting addresses default exposure. Enforceability varies by jurisdiction, which is why netting opinions are obtained jurisdiction by jurisdiction.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement
cards.reading: Reading 94: Gregory, ISDA Master Agreement, Netting and Close-out
cards.statement: Close-out netting permits the non-defaulting party to enforce only those transactions that are favourable to it and to repudiate the rest, which is what produces the exposure reduction.
cards.explanation: Selectively enforcing favourable transactions and repudiating the rest is cherry-picking by an insolvency administrator, which is exactly what close-out netting exists to prevent by collapsing all transactions to one net amount.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement
cards.reading: Reading 94: Gregory, ISDA Master Agreement, Netting and Close-out
cards.statement: Multilateral netting is available bilaterally under any ISDA Master Agreement, since the agreement covers all transactions between the two parties and can be extended to third parties by notice.
cards.explanation: An ISDA Master Agreement is bilateral by construction and cannot be extended to third parties by notice. Multilateral netting requires all participants to face the same counterparty, generally a CCP.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
